- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥1.0) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly, especially in early/medium horizon.
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤-1.0), model underestimates; adjust upward, particularly if price is trending down.
- Model often overshoots after sharp upward spikes in sentiment; cap forecast at 1–2% below true peak in next 5–7 days.
- In mean-reversion scenarios (sentiment oscillates), model overreacts to short-term noise; smooth out forecast by averaging last 3–5 days’ values.
- For 30-day horizon, model frequently underestimates late-period price increases; add 0.5–1.5% buffer to final 5–7 days if sentiment is bullish.
- If sentiment shifts from negative to positive mid-horizon, model lags in adjusting; apply early correction to avoid prolonged underestimation.
- Avoid forecasting sharp downward moves unless sentiment is strongly negative (≥3 consecutive -1.0s); model tends to underestimate downside risk.
